overview.definition: Upanishads are philosophical scriptures forming the concluding part of the Vedas and exploring ultimate reality (Brahman), the self (Atman), and liberation (moksha).
overview.meaning_of_word: Upanishad means 'sitting near the teacher' to receive secret spiritual knowledge.
overview.primary_goal: Realization of the unity between Atman and Brahman.

major_philosophical_concepts.definition: Ultimate universal reality and source of all existence.
Inner self or soul identical with Brahman.
Liberation from cycle of birth and death.

rigveda_associated.name: Aitareya Upanishad
rigveda_associated.focus: Creation of universe and consciousness as ultimate reality

rigveda_associated.name: Kaushitaki Upanishad
rigveda_associated.focus: Nature of the soul and journey after death

samaveda_associated.name: Kena Upanishad
samaveda_associated.focus: Mystery behind the power of mind and senses

yajurveda_associated.name: Isha Upanishad
yajurveda_associated.focus: Unity of divine presence in universe

yajurveda_associated.name: Taittiriya Upanishad
yajurveda_associated.focus: Five layers of human existence (Pancha Kosha)

yajurveda_associated.name: Katha Upanishad
yajurveda_associated.focus: Dialogue between Nachiketa and Yama about death

atharvaveda_associated.name: Mandukya Upanishad
atharvaveda_associated.focus: Philosophy of OM and states of consciousness

importance_in_philosophy.vedanta_foundation: Upanishads form the philosophical base for Vedanta schools.
importance_in_philosophy.influence_on_hinduism: They shaped spiritual ideas such as yoga, meditation, and self-realization.
